description: Join us for our Stem Cell Genome Engineering Series | Organoid Models, which highlights advances in genome engineering for stem cell biology and therapeutic development, aligning with our vision to Discover, Engineer, Heal. At our Nov 10 session, we will hear from speaker Michelle Gbenedio, who will present "Patient-Derived Organoid Resources: From 3D Model Development to Disease Modeling and Drug Screening." Advances in organoid technology have offered new opportunities for studying human biology and disease in vitro. In collaboration with UCSF clinicians, the Organoid Core has established a living organoid biobank of over 100 organoid lines to serve as a platform for collaborative research at UCSF. The talk will cover how these 3D models are generated and used for downstream applications like genomic and biomarker analyses as well as testing therapeutic responses. Speaker Lineup | Fall 2026 Oct 13 | Dan Wagner | Single-Cell Genomics: From Cell Atlases to Genotype-Resolved Biology Oct 27 | James Gardner | Normothermic perfusion systems as platforms for groundbreaking ex vivo human biology Nov 10 | Michelle Gbenedio | Patient-Derived Organoid Resources: From 3D Model Development to Disease Modeling and Drug Screening Dec 8 | Alex Pollen | Experimental and analytical techniques for village culture organoids UCSF welcomes all participants to our events. description: Explore How Nursing Research Is Shaping Climate and Health Education and Policy! On Tuesday, November 10th (7:00 a.m. to 7:30 a.m. Pacific Time), please join the Center for Global Nursing to welcome Ashley Moore, PhD, RN, Registered Nurse at the UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center, as our featured speaker for the November Global Nursing Impact Series. Dr. Moore will share insights from the global nursing survey she spearheaded for the Lancet Countdown 2026, examining the integration of climate and planetary health into nursing education globally and its implications for nursing education and policy. Please click here to register. Following registration, you will receive an email from the Center for Global Nursing (noreply@zoom.us) with your unique link to join the webinar, Webinar ID, Participant ID, and passcode. Please save this email, as you will need your unique link to access the webinar. A 2025–2026 Climate and Planetary Health Nursing Fellow with the Global Consortium on Climate and Health Education at Columbia University’s Mailman School of Public Health, Dr. Moore contributes to international efforts to strengthen climate and planetary health education and better prepare nurses and other healthcare professionals to respond to climate-related health challenges. Dr. Moore’s work spans oncology, women’s health, global health policy, disaster response, and climate and planetary health. Her doctoral research examined the impact of climate-driven disasters on women’s health and well-being, including the 2023 Watsonville and Pájaro floods in California, with a focus on community recovery, institutional response, and access to care. Grounded in her experience as a registered nurse, her work brings together clinical practice, global health, and planetary health, with a particular focus on strengthening nursing leadership in the face of a changing climate. She also serves as faculty for CGN’s Certificate in Global Nursing Program.

description: Gains and Losses: Navigating Skeletal Health in the Era of Rapid Weight Loss Interventions Although weight loss interventions such as metabolic surgery, anti-obesity medications, and caloric restriction can improve metabolic health, they have unintended consequences on skeletal integrity. This Grand Rounds will examine the mechanisms linking weight loss to accelerated bone remodeling and changes in bone density, quality, and fracture risk. The session will examine the implications of weight loss interventions for skeletal health, reviewing evidence-based strategies for monitoring and preserving bone strength during weight reduction. Speaker: Anne Schafer, MD, is a professor of medicine and chief of the Division of Endocrinology and Metabolism at the San Francisco VA Health Care System. She also holds a secondary appointment in the Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics. Her research focuses on osteoporosis and bone metabolism, including the effects of obesity, diabetes, and bariatric surgery on skeletal health. She was named a fellow of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research in 2025. How to Attend: In Person: S-214, Medical Sciences Building (513 Parnassus Avenue) Lunch will be provided Virtually: https://lecture.ucsf.edu/mediasite/Channel/8557b65a7d0443d6bbfa181e1bd798075f New procedures for claiming CME credit: Please review this informational guide on the updated ways to claim CME credit.

description: 8-Week Mindfulness-Based Cancer Recovery Program Online Zoom program, with Valeria Galetto, PhD If you have received a cancer diagnosis, you know the emotional part can take a toll on you. Research shows that if you learn how to manage your stress and anxiety, you can improve your quality of life and become an active participant in your own recovery and survivorship. This program is based on Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR), a therapeutic combination of mindfulness meditation, gentle yoga, and simple practices designed to let go of fears and concerns and focus on getting well. Please plan to attend all nine sessions (Including the Saturday Session). The mindfulness subject matter builds from one session to the next, so it is important that attendees can commit to at least 6 of the 8 class sessions to participate. Should these dates not be convenient, please reach out for alternative support at 415-885-3693. description: Making Health Promotion Meaningful: Community-engaged Strategies for Reaching Diverse Priority Populations Presented by Simona C. Kwon, DrPH, MPH Simona C. Kwon, DrPH, MPH, is an associate professor in the Department of Population Health at NYU Grossman School of Medicine and serves as director of the NYU Center for the Study of Asian American Health. She is nationally recognized for her expertise in community-based participatory research (CBPR) and health equity initiatives aimed at reducing health disparities in immigrant and minority populations. Dr. Kwon’s research focuses on chronic disease prevention, cultural competency in healthcare, and the social determinants of health. She has led multiple NIH-funded projects addressing health issues in underserved communities, with a particular focus on Asian American populations. As a leader in public health, Dr. Kwon collaborates with community-based organizations to design and implement culturally tailored interventions. Her work highlights the importance of building trust and partnerships between healthcare systems and the communities they serve. She has published extensively on CBPR methodologies and health equity frameworks. Dr. Kwon is committed to advancing inclusive and equitable approaches to improving health outcomes across diverse populations. Learning Objectives: At the end of this activity, learners will be able to: Apply key principles of social marketing and cultural adaptation that can inform efforts to close gaps between current and ideal practice in health promotion and disease prevention for reaching priority populations. Describe how community engagement, participatory approaches, and cultural relevance can support more whole-person, integrated care through clinical practice, research, and education for diverse priority populations. Identify broad strategies for adapting evidence-based health programs to improve relevance, implementation, and sustainability in priority communities, with the goal of improving health outcomes. Accreditation Statement Continuing Education: This UCSF continuing education activity was planned and developed to: uphold academic standards to ensure balance, independence, objectivity, and scientific rigor; adhere to requirements to protect health information under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA); and, include a mechanism to inform learners when unapproved or unlabeled uses of therapeutic products or agents are discussed or referenced. UCSF adheres to the ACCME’s Standards for Integrity and Independence in Accredited Continuing Education. Any individuals in a position to control the content of a CE activity, including content planners, reviewers, authors, presenters, moderators, panelists, or others are required to disclose all financial relationships with ineligible entities. All relevant financial relationships have been mitigated prior to the commencement of the activity. Accreditation: In support of improving patient care, the University of California, San Francisco Office of Continuing Medical Education (CME) is jointly accredited by the Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME), the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE), and the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), to provide continuing education for the healthcare team. This CME activity meets the requirements under California Assembly 1195, continuing education, and cultural and linguistic competency.
